newsitem.title: CHINA: China's Baoshi to post lower H1 '97 net.
newsitem.headline: China's Baoshi to post lower H1 '97 net.

text.p: Shijiazhuang Baoshi Electronic Co Ltd said on Thursday it would post lower net profits for first half of 1997 due to a sluggish domestic television tube market.

The company, one of China's biggest black-and-white television tube makers, posted unaudited net profits of 65.66 million yuan for January-June 1996, down 20.7 percent from 82.75 million yuan in the year-earlier period.

"The domestic black-and-white tube market remains weak. The sales price of colour television tubes also dropped in the first half," the spokeswoman told the Hong Kong-based newsletter China Securities Bulletin.
Interest payments on loans for investment in the company's colour television tube production line had also cut into profits, she said.
"Considering these factors, Baoshi should report lower profits for the first half," the official said, but declined to give an estimate.
Baoshi would make public its interim results around mid-August, she added.
Baoshi has said it invested about 2.7 billion yuan in the production of colour television tubes, of which 1.7 billion to 1.8 billion yuan were borrowed from banks.
The firm started producing colour tubes last July. But the sector generated little profit in 1996, hurt by a savage price war among China's colour television makers, Baoshi said.

Baoshi, which listed 100 million hard currency B shares in July 1996, booked 82.47 million yuan in net profits in 1996, down 52.17 percent from 172.43 million yuan for 1995 under Chinese accounting standards.
Figures using international standards were not available.
